title: Moved-Load Relief in the Recalculation of a Security Deposit
content:
When a member's load has moved to other meters, the member's record on those other meters earns a moved-load relief in the recalculation of a held Security Deposits deposit.

## Terms

The moved-load relief reads the member's other service accounts — every Electric Service by Rate Schedule account of the member other than the one the deposit secures — over the last twelve whole months. Payments on them with no late payment charge and every one by automatic bank draft earn the full moved-load relief of **0.10**; payments on them with no late payment charge but not all by bank draft earn the part moved-load relief of **0.05**; otherwise none. The moved-load relief is taken off the recalculation multiple. The recalculation multiple is never below **1.0**; that floor is applied once, to the multiple as finally reckoned.

## Combinations

| Service payments on the other accounts | Late payment charges on the other accounts | Every payment by automatic bank draft | Relief |
|---|---|---|---|
| at least one | none | yes | 0.10 |
| at least one | none | no | 0.05 |
| at least one | one or more | either | none |
| none | any | — | none |

## Hypothetical illustration

A member's farm home deposit is recalculated; the member's shop meter and irrigation pivot together show nine payments in the last twelve months, all by bank draft, and no late payment charge: the relief is 0.10. Had one of those payments come by mailed check, it would be 0.05; had the pivot been billed one late payment charge, none.
